back: Anything an enterprise owns or controls and uses to produce goods and services; tangible (physical) or intangible (not physical).
What an enterprise can do by combining and using its resources well, e.g. fast delivery or reliable quality.
A skill or strength that customers value, rivals find hard to copy, and that can be used in more than one product or market.
Tangible: land, buildings, machines, stock. Intangible: brand, skills, licences, goodwill.
Hire suits short-term or occasional use and low capital; purchase suits long, frequent use. Compare total cost over the expected years of use.
A developer builds a facility, owns it and earns income for an agreed period, then transfers ownership to the client.
As BOT, but the developer also operates the facility during the period before handing it over.
Avoid waste, maintain equipment, share assets and reuse materials.
Using resources no faster than they renew so the enterprise can continue for the long term.
